pulse: Stocks pulled back on 2026-11-16, with the S&P 500 off 0.40% to 7561.67 and the Nasdaq 100 down 1.22% to 27943.74 as chipmakers sold off, while the Dow Jones eked out a 0.10% gain to 52347.55 and the Russell 2000 slipped 0.31% to 2790.49. Breadth was actually positive beneath the index-level weakness, with 313 advancers versus 187 decliners among S&P 500 names. Electronic Technology was the weakest sector (-2.07%) dragged down by semiconductor names, alongside Consumer Durables (-1.51%) and Producer Manufacturing (-1.41%), while Consumer Non-Durables (+1.45%) and Energy Minerals (+1.00%) led gainers. The VIX spiked 6.11% to 20.48 reflecting the risk-off tone, the 10-year yield eased 0.19% to 5.129%, the dollar (DXY) was roughly flat at 103.464 (+0.05%), WTI crude fell 0.85% to $87.81, and Bitcoin dropped 1.86% to $64,096.66. Among the most-active names, AMD led decliners with an 8.75% plunge to $534.06 on volume of 49.4 million, Broadcom (AVGO) fell 4.76% to $347.01, and Nvidia (NVDA) slid 2.01% to $162.85 on heavy volume of 365.8 million shares, while Meta (META) was the standout gainer, up 2.90% to $641.69.
